To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the equation of state of neutron matter is well described by chiral EFT up to one and half times saturation density, and that the momentum distribution is in good agreement with the experimental data.
we have performed the first fully nonperturbitive quantum Monte Carlo calculations with a nonlocal chiral EFT potential for the ground-state of neutron matter.
quantum Monte Carlo calculations with nonlocal effective interactions provide a benchmark for ab initio calculations of neutron matter and the equation of state of neutron matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear matter using the ab initio many-body theory.
the development of new methods to calculate the properties of strongly interacting matter, and with their application to nuclear systems.
the development of new computational techniques for solving the quantum many-body problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlocal chiral EFT approach is a promising and viable approach to the nuclear equation of state, but it is not yet fully mature.
the chiral EFT approach to nuclear structure is now in the process of being established as a reliable tool for nuclear physics.

the nonlocal chiral EFT calculations are able to describe the equation of state of neutron matter at densities relevant for the neutron star interior, and that they are able to describe nuclear matter saturation properties at the 10% level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the chiral effective theory can be used to calculate the equation of state of neutron matter and the neutron chemical potential.
, we have shown how to use the nonlocal chiral EFT to calculate the equation of state of neutron matter, and the equation of state is consistent with the experimental data.
we have performed the first fully nonperturbatively converged quantum Monte Carlo calculations for nuclear matter with a chiral effective field-theory interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the equation of state of pure neutron matter is well reproduced by the chiral EFT at next-to-next- to-leading order, and that this is a promising starting point for the study of nuclear matter with chiral EFT.
the equation of state of neutron matter is not sensitive to the choice of chiral EPT interaction at the next-to-next-to leading order.
the nonlocality of the chiral EFT potential is crucial to obtain accurate neutron matter calculations at low densities.
